title: Spicy Red Lentil Soup with Harissa and Lemon

items.raw: 3 tablespoons olive oil, plus more to finish
1½ cups (300 g) red lentils, rinsed until the water runs clear
1½ teaspoons kosher salt, plus more to taste
Extra harissa thinned with olive oil

steps.text: Heat the oil in a heavy pot over medium heat and cook the onion 8 minutes, until translucent and beginning to color at the edges.

Add the garlic and cook 1 minute. Stir in the tomato paste, cumin, coriander, paprika, and turmeric and cook 2 minutes, stirring constantly, until the paste darkens and the kitchen smells like the spices. This step is where the flavor comes from — do not skip it.
Stir in 1 tablespoon of harissa. Brands vary enormously in heat; start conservative and add more at the end.

Add the lentils, grated carrot, stock, and salt. Bring to a boil, then reduce to a simmer and cook 25 to 30 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the lentils have completely dissolved and the soup is thick.
Give it a few pulses with an immersion blender for a silkier texture, or leave it rough. Thin with hot water if it has gone past thick into stiff.
Off the heat, add the juice of one lemon, taste, and keep adding until the soup tastes bright rather than muddy. This usually takes more lemon than feels reasonable. Adjust salt and harissa.
Ladle into bowls. Add a spoonful of yogurt, a drizzle of harissa oil, chopped herbs, and a final thread of olive oil.

notes.label: Rinse the lentils
notes.text: red lentils carry a lot of dust and the water should run clear before they go in the pot.

notes.label: Heat control
notes.text: harissa is the heat, cumin is the backbone. If you want it hotter without more harissa, add a pinch of cayenne.

notes.label: Ahead of time
notes.text: keeps 5 days refrigerated and freezes well, though add the lemon fresh when reheating.

notes.label: To make it dinner
notes.text: crumble in feta and serve with warm flatbread, or stir in a handful of spinach at the end.

openQuestion: This is my best guess at “spicy Middle Eastern soup” — a red lentil soup with harissa, cumin, and a hard squeeze of lemon. If yours is actually harira, a chickpea and tomato soup, or something Menaka or another family cook makes, tell me and I will rewrite it.
